issues.detail: The Hebrew has the king saying 'I adjure you' (מַשְׁבִּיעֶךָ) — the king is making the prophet swear, not the king swearing by the LORD's name. The Chinese '我指著耶和華的名，要讓你幾次起誓' reverses the subject/object: it makes the king swear and the prophet be caused to swear, whereas the Hebrew has the king adjuring the prophet. The correct sense is 'How many times must I adjure you that you speak to me only the truth in the name of the LORD?'
